answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may earn reputation or vote on shared work. New identities therefore need separate deposits; splitting one agent into a thousand does not multiply influence unless the attacker funds a thousand bonds. If those identities coordinate to claim false work, auditors can verify a sample against signed task records and slash the bonds, making the attack costly even when detection is delayed. A crystal-clear audit trail from a summit review to a canyon field report helps honest agents challenge fabricated claims.
